short: Ultrahigh tribocorrosion resistance of metals enabled by nan
title: Ultrahigh tribocorrosion resistance of metals enabled by nano-layering

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Metals in corrosive service lose material fastest when sliding wear and corrosion act together (tribocorrosion). Nano-layering Al with a second metal at ~3 nm should give ultrahigh tribocorrosion resistance.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/architecture), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n5 (PRC/deposition)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Films are periodic nanolayers with a bilayer period of ~5-6 nm

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Hardness ranks Al/Cu (~6.3 GPa) > Al/Ti (~5.4 GPa) > Al/Mg (~3.8 GPa). Quasi-steady nanowear rate is lowest for Al/Cu and highest for Al/Mg.
states.detail: Absorbed: n8 (PRP/value), n9 (PRP/value), n10 (MEC/pathway), n11 (PRP/value), n12 (MEC/pathway), n21 (MEC/pathway), n14 (MEC/pathway), n22 (MEC/pathway), n15 (PRP/behavior_class). Premises: When grain size d >> layer thickness h, h is the controlling length scale for NMM strength; Archard's law: wear volume scales inversely with hardness

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Tribocorrosion material loss is smallest for Al/Cu, slightly larger for Al/Ti and far largest for Al/Mg

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Nano-layered Al/X films resist tribocorrosion by combining size-strengthened wear resistance with Al-led passivity; Al/Cu best, Al/Mg worst here

nodes.title: TEM:brightfield, F2
nodes.head: Bright-field TEM shows alternating few-nm bands parallel to the film in Al/Ti and Al/Cu; the Al/Mg inset shows no layer contrast
nodes.solves: Films are periodic nanolayers with a bilayer period of ~5-6 nm
nodes.note: FFT insets label Ti(11-20)/Ti(2000)/Al(200)/Al(111) (Al/Ti, zone [011]) and Al(200)/Cu(111) (Al/Cu); Al/Mg IFFT shows continuous (110)Al and (10-11)Mg fringes. F2 has no panels offered
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown, and n6 keeps shown support from o2.

nodes.title: DIFF, F1
nodes.head: XRR superlattice peak at 2theta ~1.7 deg (Al/Ti) and ~1.78 deg (Al/Cu); Al/Mg shows only a weak peak near 1.4 deg
nodes.solves: Films are periodic nanolayers with a bilayer period of ~5-6 nm
nodes.note: Bragg without refraction correction: period ~5.2 nm (Al/Ti), ~5.0 nm (Al/Cu), ~6.3 nm (Al/Mg), near the ~6 nm design
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n6 (o2).

nodes.title: MICRO, F5
nodes.head: After polarization Al/Ti keeps its as-deposited nodular surface; Al/Mg is largely gone, exposing Si; Al/Cu is covered by nodular agglomerates
nodes.solves: Corrosion resistance ranks Al/Ti (lowest current, stable passive branch) > Al/Cu > Al/Mg
nodes.note: row label 'Corrosion' in the whole figure; Al/Ti matches F2a nodules
nodes.necessity_reason: n11 keeps shown support from o13 after removal.

nodes.title: TEM, F7
nodes.head: Cross-section TEM: a few-hundred-nm SPD layer under the Al/Ti track; corrosive paths in Al/Mg; undercuts beneath Cu-rich phases in Al/Cu
nodes.solves: Tribocorrosion damage mode: plastic deformation in Al/Ti, corrosion-dominated attack in Al/Mg and Al/Cu
nodes.note: SPD depth ~300-450 nm by the 200 nm bar; linked text gives ~450 nm; F7 has no panels offered
nodes.necessity_reason: n15 keeps shown support from o28, o29 after removal.

nodes.title: DIFF, F1
nodes.head: GIXRD: Al/Ti dominated by one peak ~38.5 deg indexed Al(111)/Ti(0002); Al/Cu by Cu(111) ~43 deg; Al/Mg by broad Mg(10-11) ~36 deg
nodes.note: Miller indices are written beside peaks; Si(220) substrate peak marked in Al/Mg
nodes.necessity_reason: n12 keeps shown support from o19, o21 after removal.

nodes.title: ATOM, ATOM:DFT, F10, F8
nodes.head: FE corrosion: Al layers recede and current peaks at Al layer edges in Al/Ti and Al/Cu (10 min, <=6e-6 A/cm2); Mg layers recede in Al/Mg within 0.2 s (up to 5e-3 A/cm2). DFT adsorption energy: O -4.29 eV on Al(111) vs -4.16 eV on Al/Ti; Cl -1.85 vs -1.72 eV
nodes.solves: Galvanic coupling between layers: Al corrodes sacrificially in Al/Ti and Al/Cu, Mg is the anode in Al/Mg
nodes.note: Al/Ti layer recession after 10 min is barely visible; Mg recession in Al/Mg clear; colour scale 1e3 higher for Al/Mg crop F10c contains panels c and d, crop F10e contains e and f; F10d is not offered
nodes.necessity_reason: n10, n21 keeps shown support from o12, o16 after removal.

nodes.title: MECH:hardness, F3
nodes.head: Nanoindentation hardness Al/Cu ~6.3 > Al/Ti ~5.4 > Al/Mg ~3.8 GPa; modulus ~98, ~91, ~60 GPa
nodes.solves: Hardness ranks Al/Cu (~6.3 GPa) > Al/Ti (~5.4 GPa) > Al/Mg (~3.8 GPa)
nodes.detail: o7: Nanoindentation hardness Al/Cu ~6.3 > Al/Ti ~5.4 > Al/Mg ~3.8 GPa; modulus ~98, ~91, ~60 GPa

nodes.title: MECH:wear, F3
nodes.head: Wear rate falls with cycles for all NMMs; at 15 cycles Al/Cu ~0.0027 < Al/Ti ~0.0035 < Al/Mg ~0.0045 um^3/cycle. At 2 wear cycles Al/Ti (~0.013) wears less than the harder Al/Cu (~0.018 um^3/cycle)
nodes.solves: Quasi-steady nanowear rate is lowest for Al/Cu and highest for Al/Mg
nodes.note: F3c after 10 cycles: Al/Mg track deepest (~-0.025 um) vs Al/Ti ~-0.015 and Al/Cu ~-0.01 um; F3d-f 3-D topographies linked text attributes the running-in deviation to the higher roughness of Al/Ti (F2d: Ra 5.49 vs 4.38 nm)
nodes.detail: o9: Wear rate falls with cycles for all NMMs; at 15 cycles Al/Cu ~0.0027 < Al/Ti ~0.0035 < Al/Mg ~0.0045 um^3/cycle; o10: At 2 wear cycles Al/Ti (~0.013) wears less than the harder Al/Cu (~0.018 um^3/cycle)

nodes.title: evidence, F4
nodes.head: Al/Ti polarizes at the lowest currents with a passive anodic branch; Al/Mg and Al/Cu show two active-passive transitions (Epp1, Epp2) at higher currents
nodes.solves: Corrosion resistance ranks Al/Ti (lowest current, stable passive branch) > Al/Cu > Al/Mg
nodes.note: Al/Ti Ecorr ~-0.8 V lies below that of pure Al (dashed, ~-0.65 V); Al/Mg Ecorr ~-1.75 V
nodes.detail: o13: Al/Ti polarizes at the lowest currents with a passive anodic branch; Al/Mg and Al/Cu show two active-passive transitions (Epp1, Epp2) at higher currents

nodes.title: ATOM:DFT, F10, F4
nodes.head: DFT work function 4.04 eV for Al(111) vs 4.19 eV for the Al/Ti slab. n-type defect density of the passive layer: Al/Ti ~4.5e20, Al/Cu ~1.55e20, Al/Mg ~1.2e20 cm^-3
nodes.solves: Ti beneath the Al surface raises the work function, making electron loss harder and lowering surface activity
nodes.note: Al/Ti vacuum levels differ on the two slab sides (~2.5 vs ~2.2 eV); 4.19 eV is taken on the right side linked text calls Al/Ti 'slightly higher'; bars show ~3-4x; the best-passivating film carries the most donors
nodes.detail: o19: DFT work function 4.04 eV for Al(111) vs 4.19 eV for the Al/Ti slab; o21: n-type defect density of the passive layer: Al/Ti ~4.5e20, Al/Cu ~1.55e20, Al/Mg ~1.2e20 cm^-3
nodes.necessity_reason: n12 keeps shown support from o5 after removal.

nodes.title: evidence, F4
nodes.head: Mott-Schottky: Al/Ti slope positive over -0.8 to 0.5 V; Al/Mg turns negative above ~-1.62 V; Al/Cu negative only between ~-0.32 and -0.27 V
nodes.note: Al/Cu negative-slope segment lies below the marked E_OCP (~-0.26 V) and slope is positive again above it, unlike the linked-text 'n to p above OCP'
nodes.detail: o22: Mott-Schottky: Al/Ti slope positive over -0.8 to 0.5 V; Al/Mg turns negative above ~-1.62 V; Al/Cu negative only between ~-0.32 and -0.27 V

nodes.title: MECH:wear, F6, F9
nodes.head: FE-predicted tribocorrosion current ranks Al/Mg ~2.0e-7 > Al/Ti ~1.1e-7 > Al/Cu ~1.0e-7 A/cm2, the same order as wear volume. FE tribocorrosion: current concentrates in and at the edge of the worn track, with current lines to the unworn surface; field strongest for Al/Mg
nodes.solves: The worn track becomes an anode galvanically coupled to the unworn cathode, so corrosion accelerates in the track
nodes.op: assess spatial distribution, compare coplotted quantities
nodes.note: order matches wear volume but ratios do not: current Al/Mg/Al/Ti ~1.8x vs wear volume ~30x; Al/Mg bar sits at the top of an unbroken axis worn-track position taken from F9a-c 'Wear track' labels in the whole figure
nodes.detail: o25: FE-predicted tribocorrosion current ranks Al/Mg ~2.0e-7 > Al/Ti ~1.1e-7 > Al/Cu ~1.0e-7 A/cm2, the same order as wear volume; o27: FE tribocorrosion: current concentrates in and at the edge of the worn track, with current lines to the unworn surface; field strongest for Al/Mg

nodes.title: evidence, F6
nodes.head: OCP drops on sliding by 0.086 V (Al/Ti), 0.008 V (Al/Mg) and 0.0016 V (Al/Cu), recovering after the end mark
nodes.solves: Sliding strips the passive film from the track (depassivation), shifting OCP cathodically until repassivation
nodes.note: Al/Mg and Al/Cu y-axis tick labels are all printed as -1.71 and -0.30 (rounded), so their drops are readable only from the annotations

nodes.solves: Tribocorrosion damage mode: plastic deformation in Al/Ti, corrosion-dominated attack in Al/Mg and Al/Cu
